text:
Marie Chen: quick design review — new regression-diff list for eval runs is in the prototype. want UX eyes on the compact vs. expanded rows and the approve CTA copy
Samir Patel: looking now. is this the list that shows diffs for prompt sets + scorecard regressions?
Marie Chen: yep. one row per failing prompt + a small inline diff preview. main debate: should we collapse long diffs by default, or show full snippets?
Jon Reyes: collapse by default, with a 'Show full diff' affordance. large diffs are noisy during quick triage.
Tara Liu: +1 on collapse. but add an accessible toggle and ensure keyboard focus lands on the toggle. also we need clear SR (screen reader) text that reads "Show full diff for prompt X"
Marie Chen: noted. also copy for the primary CTA — currently says "Accept change". product wants clearer language for review flows. any alternatives?
Samir Patel: what about "Approve as baseline" vs "Mark as approved"? "Accept change" feels ambiguous.
Jon Reyes: "Approve as baseline" is more explicit but long. "Approve" alone might be too terse.
Tara Liu: prefer short + explicit: "Approve baseline" or "Confirm baseline". either way, we need a confirm modal for bulk actions. accidental approvals are dangerous.
Marie Chen: design suggestion: primary button = "Approve baseline"; secondary = "Request change"; bulk action shows a 2-step confirm with number of prompts listed.
Samir Patel: technical note: bulk confirm should include a keyboard shortcut and `aria-describedby` pointing to the summary list. avoid modal traps.
Jon Reyes: for the list layout: add a small failed-score badge (red) and a visual regression sparkline. keep row height minimal. we can hide the sparkline on mobile.
Tara Liu: color contrast for the red badge is failing at small sizes. a11y-bot: run results attached.
a11y-bot: Automated scan: 3 contrast issues found on this screen: failed-score badge (WCAG AA), empty-state CTA contrast, and focus outline visibility on dropdown toggles. See https://a11y.scans/scan/4821
Marie Chen: thanks bot. Tara, can you propose accessible color tokens? Samir, shallow CSS change ok?
Tara Liu: proposing token `--color-attention-600` with 4.5:1 contrast to white for small text. will post sample swatches in figma.
Samir Patel: should be fine, but need to run visual regression on other places using that token. I can add a storybook knob and a test.
Jon Reyes: another microcopy nit: the inline diff preview shows `+`/`-` markers but no legend. users asked for an inline legend tooltip.
Marie Chen: add a small helper text: "+ added text · - removed text" visible on hover/focus. also keyboard-accessible via `?` shortcut in the view.
Tara Liu: keyboard nav plan: Tab to row, Enter expands, Space toggles selection, Shift+Arrow to multi-select. ensure focus styles are >=3px visible outline.
Samir Patel: implementation note: use `role="list"` and `role="listitem"` for rows; add `aria-expanded` on the expand toggle; keep DOM order linear so SR reads row then actions.
Jon Reyes: regarding routing from diff to affected prompt set: include a contextual link "Open prompt" that opens console panel. need to ensure it opens in current workspace tab, not a new window.
Marie Chen: UX question: should we show an inline severity filter (High/Medium/Low) at the top? designers feel it helps triage.
Tara Liu: yes, with clear label "Severity" and accessible toggle buttons. use `role=tablist` or `radiogroup`? radiogroup may be better for exclusive filter.
Samir Patel: radiogroup is fine. we'll implement with buttons and `aria-pressed` state and ensure it works with arrow keys.
Marie Chen: copy for empty state when no regressions: current text "No diffs detected" — PM suggested something more action-oriented. ideas?
Jon Reyes: "No regressions found — your baseline is current. Run an eval to compare changes." keep it short. add a button "Run eval" and a secondary link "View history".
Tara Liu: add hidden SR-only text: "No regressions detected for the selected prompt set and time range."
Marie Chen: final asks: 1) Tara — color tokens + accessibility checklist; 2) Samir — PR and storybook tests; 3) Jon — tiny visual tweaks and legend tooltip. I'll file the design tasks in Figma and link the PR when ready.
Samir Patel: assigning to me. will open branch `fe/evals/diff-list-compact` and add tests. ETA EOW.
Jon Reyes: i'll add the tooltip component and spritemap changes.
Tara Liu: will post contrast swatches and aria notes by EOD.
Marie Chen: awesome. last convo: can we tweak CTA hover focus to use an inner shadow rather than heavy color shift? accessibility-wise focus must be distinct, but not solely color.
Samir Patel: ok — we'll use a 3px outline + subtle inner shadow. I'll attach CSS snippet in the PR:
```
.button:focus { outline: 3px solid var(--focus-ring); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.04); }
```
Marie Chen: perfect. thanks everyone :rocket:
